title: Chapter 75
content:
[President Kang, I like you! I've never experienced such sublime, incredible sex in my entire life!]

The shrill, looping recording drilled straight into Jakyeong’s skull, wrenching his eyes open with a string of vicious curses. Thinking it was a lingering nightmare, he jolted upright, scanning the room—only to spot Kang Il-hyun’s phone resting on the nightstand, blaring the audio on full volume.

Did that psychotic bastard actually set my frantic begging as his morning alarm?

Fuming, Jakyeong lunged to snatch the device, but a large hand intervened, plucking it away effortlessly. Fresh from the shower, Il-hyun stood draped in a plush bathrobe, a damp towel slung lazily over his dark hair.

Silencing the alarm with a swipe of his thumb, Il-hyun broke into a bright grin, leaning down to plant a sudden, sweet peck on Jakyeong’s parted lips.

"Sleep well, darling?"

He reached out, affectionately ruffling Jakyeong’s messy bedhead. Jakyeong slapped the hand away, glaring daggers.

"Delete that right now."

"Delete what?"

"The goddamn recording!"

"Why? It's like music to my ears."

When Il-hyun threatened to replay the loop, Jakyeong grabbed his pillow, hurling it with homicidal force. Drop dead! The sudden exertion sent a sharp, tearing ache radiating up his lower spine, collapsing him back onto the mattress with a stifled groan. Getting tossed around in bed was proving far more physically grueling than running tactical field contracts.

Seeing him immobilized, Il-hyun slid onto the mattress, lying on his side to study Jakyeong’s profile with unblinking amusement.

Jakyeong stared up at the ceiling, blinking in silent defeat.

Unlike his own battered, aching frame, Kang Il-hyun looked positively glowing—as if a single night of debauchery had shaved years off his life. The vivid memory of the man pinning him down, unhinged with arousal as he came across Jakyeong’s face, flashed behind his eyelids. Previously, their encounters had felt like one-sided violations; last night, he had actively surrendered and played along.

I've completely lost my mind. Truly, utterly insane.

It felt like crossing an irreversible Rubicon.

Noticing the sudden, brooding shadow crossing Jakyeong's face, Il-hyun gently brushed the dark fringe from the boy's forehead.

"Alright, alright. I'll delete it. Don't pout."

"..."

"Want to sleep a bit longer?"

"No."

"Shall we head out for breakfast, then?"

Considering it was already creeping past noon, calling it breakfast was a stretch. Yet despite the physical exhaustion, last night’s intense exertion had left his stomach completely hollow. When Il-hyun caught his wrist, coaxing him off the bed, Jakyeong reluctantly let himself be dragged onto his feet.

Slipping into the bathroom, he shed his robe to inspect the damage. His skin was a mottled canvas of purples and pinks. Taking in his swollen, bruised nipples, he shook his head in bitter disgust—the man was a verified degenerate.

Under the hot stream of the shower, the sticky remnants of Il-hyun's release slicked down his inner thighs.

Jakyeong stared down in numb, paralyzed shock. Tipping his head back against the marble tiles, he let out a long, heavy exhale.

Just look at the bright side. You got off too. You didn't hate it.

Yet a horrifying thought crept in: At this rate, am I going to end up straddling the bastard and riding him of my own free will? The sheer prospect sent a wave of despair crashing over him.

After scrubbing down thoroughly with cold water, he pulled on a casual outfit and stepped into the living room.

Il-hyun was lounging on the sofa, sipping tea. Dressed in tailored linen shorts, a loose button-down, and dark designer sunglasses, the vacation attire felt completely foreign on a corporate predator who usually lived in bespoke three-piece suits. His exposed calves were long, lean, and densely corded with muscle, making the casual look appear effortlessly striking.

Jakyeong inadvertently scanned him from head to toe—a visual sweep Il-hyun caught instantly.

Spreading his arms wide with a boyish grin, Il-hyun preened. "Like what you see?"

Jakyeong turned his back, feigning total indifference, but Il-hyun shadowed his heels, pestering him relentlessly for a compliment. Annoyed by the badgering, Jakyeong gave a begrudging nod, prompting Il-hyun to run a hand through his hair with radiant, insufferable pride. When arrogance was entirely backed by undeniable physical perfection, it was impossible to scoff—which only made it ten times more infuriating.

Stepping outside, Jakyeong finally took in the villa’s exterior. It was a rustic, sun-bleached timber cottage—compact, charming, and clearly carrying decades of history.

It looked absurdly out of place for a billionaire syndicate heir. Why on earth did he build a retreat here?

Before he could ponder the architecture, his eyes landed on a pristine white sports car idling on the gravel drive.

"Catch," Il-hyun said, tossing a key fob through the air.

Jakyeong caught it cleanly.

"You drive, darling."

Suppressing a smile, a spark of genuine excitement lit up in his chest. He slipped into the leather bucket seat, thumbing the push-to-start. The engine roared to life with a throaty, aggressive purr that set his pulse racing.

Clearing the driveway, the road wound directly along the coastal bluffs. The asphalt was surprisingly smooth and well-maintained.

Jakyeong had expected an uninhabited rock like the one they’d fled to, but this island was expansive, boasting proper civil infrastructure. Cruising along the coastline, the crisp, salty sea breeze rushed through the open cabin.

Glancing across the console, Il-hyun had his forearm propped against the window frame, gazing out at the open water.

With his dark hair whipping freely in the wind and a relaxed, unburdened smile gracing his lips, the man looked like a frame cut straight from a high-budget European film.

Drifting smoothly around a cliffside hairpin, a quaint strip of seaside cafés and coastal bistros came into view. Seeing the empty streets, Jakyeong had worried the district was deserted, but a small boutique bistro at the end of the promenade was just flipping its sign to open.

Jakyeong pulled the roadster up to the curb. The young owner, setting out the chalkboard menu on the patio, blinked in startled awe as the two stepped out of the vehicle—clearly wondering if a pair of film stars had just arrived for an unannounced shoot.

"Are you serving lunch?"

"We are, though prep might take a moment... Will that be alright?"

Both men nodded and stepped inside. The dining room was cozy and charming, framed by panoramic windows that captured the glittering expanse of the turquoise sea beneath a cloudless sky.

While Jakyeong took in the horizon, Il-hyun flipped through the menu before sliding it across the wood.

"Done ordering?" Jakyeong asked.

"Pick for me. I have no idea what's good here."

The bistro specialized in coastal fusion pasta, incorporating locally foraged wild herbs and sea vegetables into traditional Italian sauces. As Jakyeong traced his finger down the options, he realized Il-hyun wasn't looking at the food at all—his dark eyes were pinned intently on Jakyeong’s face.

Catching the gaze, Jakyeong looked up, only for Il-hyun to offer a soft, disarmingly sweet smile.

Flustered, Jakyeong quickly placed the order with the server and took a hurried sip of iced water, keeping his eyes glued to the waves outside.

"Once we finish eating, let's hit that café I mentioned yesterday," Il-hyun noted.

Recalling the dessert spot, curiosity got the better of Jakyeong. "Do you come to this island often?"

"I used to."

"For vacations?"

Il-hyun offered a faint, melancholy smile, shaking his head. "This is where my late mother was placed for convalescence. When I was very young, I used to travel down here twice a month."

"Ah..."

"Not that she ever welcomed my presence, of course."

He delivered the tragic history with an easy, upbeat smile, mentioning he had visited a few times in his adulthood before smoothly steering the conversation toward lighter topics. Sensing the boundary, Jakyeong didn't pry further.

Once the dishes arrived, the conversation settled into an easy, surprisingly mundane rhythm.

The initial tension melted away, and Jakyeong found the sharp, defensive edge he usually maintained against Il-hyun dulling by the minute. Out in public, stripped of his corporate weapons and syndicate armor, the man behaved like a perfectly charming, ordinary human being. Whether it was another calculated mask or his genuine core was impossible to tell, but for the first time in a year, Jakyeong didn't mind the company.

Finishing lunch, they drove down to the dessert café, only to find the storefront boarded up and long abandoned. Disappointed that he wouldn't get to taste the pastries Il-hyun had hyped up, they scouted the coastline until finding a bustling, modern café overlooking the cliffs.

The venue was lively, packed with vacationing couples snapping photos over iced coffees. Self-conscious about the dark bruises and love bites mottling his throat, Jakyeong kept his collar pulled high, shielding his neck with his palm.

While waiting for their order, a young woman nervously approached their table.

"Excuse me... if you're not busy—" she began, offering a bashful smile, only to freeze mid-sentence.

Il-hyun had leaned back into his chair, fixing her with a glare so murderously cold that the air seemed to drop ten degrees on the spot.

Pale as a sheet, the woman stammered an apology and practically sprinted back to her friends.

Jakyeong let out a tired sigh. "Fix your face. You're shooting lasers out of your eyes."

"I am smiling, darling."

"No, you're not. You looked ready to snap her neck."

Il-hyun arched a single brow, his lips pulling into a dry smirk. "Why? Disappointed you didn't get her number?"

Argue with him and we'll be here all day.

Tired of the jealousy, Jakyeong folded his arms across the table, burying his face into his sleeves. Turning his head toward the panoramic glass, he closed his eyes. The ambient hum of the air conditioning, the gentle warmth of the afternoon sun on his shoulders, and the rhythmic lap of the surf lulled him into a heavy, delicious drowsiness.

Sitting across from him, Il-hyun rested his chin on his palm, his long fingers gently playing with the soft strands of Jakyeong’s hair. Deciding the touch wasn't worth fighting, Jakyeong let him be—only for those fingers to drift south, tracing the tender skin of his neck.

Feeling unusually charitable, Jakyeong allowed the indulgence.

Just as sleep was about to claim him completely, he forced himself upright.

"Exhausted?" Il-hyun asked, wearing a look of innocent concern.

Jakyeong shot him a venomous scowl. "And whose fault is that?"

"If your stamina is this fragile, how do you expect to handle field contracts? Shall I brew you some restorative tonics?"

"Save your breath. You'll just use the extra energy as an excuse to torment me more."

As the afternoon rolled in, the café grew increasingly crowded. When a second woman approached to ask for Jakyeong’s contact info—only to flee in terror after meeting Il-hyun’s demonic scowl—Jakyeong decided they had lingered long enough, hauling the possessive beast back to the roadster.

They cruised the southern bluffs until reaching an expansive luxury golf resort nestled along the cape. After an extravagant multi-course dinner at the resort’s private Italian dining room, they strolled along the private beach.

The sunset was breathtaking—the horizon catching fire in vast, brilliant ribbons of deep violet, amber, and burning crimson.

Whenever Il-hyun reached down to intertwine their fingers, Jakyeong pointedly slapped his hand away. Growing impatient, Il-hyun eventually scooped the boy up by his waist, hoisting him over his shoulder and tossing him straight into the surf.

Naturally, a furious splashing brawl ensued, ending with both of them thoroughly drenched and trading barbs all the way back to the cottage.

Pulling into the gravel drive, Il-hyun killed the engine.

As the headlights snapped off, plunging the yard into pitch-black darkness, Jakyeong grabbed a towel to wring the seawater from his hair. He reached for the door handle, only for Il-hyun’s hand to clamp firmly around his wrist.

Shh.

Il-hyun pressed an index finger to his own lips. In the gloom of the cabin, his dark irises glinted with the sharp, lethal focus of an apex predator locking onto target.

Jakyeong followed his gaze toward the timber cottage.

A moment later, Il-hyun flicked the high beams back on.

The brilliant halogen glare cut across the porch. It lasted for only a fraction of a second, but a dark silhouette flickered across the front window before vanishing into the shadows of the hallway.

An intruder.

"Did you catch that?" Il-hyun murmured.

Jakyeong stared at the darkened glass, giving a curt nod. "Do you have a sidearm in the vehicle?"

"No. Don't need one."

What does 'don't need one' even mean?

Before Jakyeong could question the lunacy, Il-hyun slammed his left foot onto the brake while pinning the throttle to the floor with his right.

The twin-turbo V8 screamed in violent protest, the tachometer needle bouncing aggressively against the redline.

Realizing the madman's plan, Jakyeong let out a weary, resigned groan, hurriedly clicking his seatbelt back into the buckle.

"Just walk through the front door like a normal person."

Il-hyun shot him a wicked wink. "Don't worry, darling. Pounding things open is my absolute specialty."

Jakyeong gagged in pure disgust. Cracking crude sexual jokes at a time like this...

"Besides," Il-hyun muttered, his jaw locking into a vicious, predatory smirk. "I never liked this goddamn house anyway."

Jakyeong braced both hands against the overhead grab handle, clenching his jaw as Il-hyun dumped the brake.

The rear tires broke traction with a concussive shriek of burning rubber, launching the white sports car straight through the front porch of the cottage like a ballistic missile.

Fucking brilliant. Where the hell are we supposed to sleep tonight?
